name: Business operations (the organisation's own running record)
one_line: How an organisation runs ITSELF, as opposed to what it sells or who works there: strategy and plans, the governance cycle, budgets and forecasts, projects and their delivery record, policies and procedures, procurement and contracts, the commercial relationship with customers and partners, product management, the IT function, and the statutory and audit evidence that proves the entity is in good standing. Its anchor is an ORGANISATIONAL UNIT running a CYCLE or a PROJECT and producing a document with a FUNCTION - not a person's own career, not a household's money, not a matter run for a client. A PLACEHOLDER SCHEMA ROW written to J-DEPTH: it declares NO field rows (D1 as narrowed, _CONTRACT rules 10 and 15, CONNECTION PR-6) and recommends NO folder dimensions, so activation unlocks recognition plus the universal facts only.

proposed_fields.example: the legal entity or internal unit whose own record this is - one company among the two a person keeps books for, or one department inside it
proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: ONE DECISION, TWO ROWS: `organization` is proposed here AND, independently and for the same reason, by the landed `construction_property` schema row, which states that it “REUSES the `organization` key already proposed by the landed business_operations schema row rather than minting a construction-flavoured variant, and it should be adjudicated once, there, for both.” R1c must therefore settle this as a single canonical-list question covering both families, not as two competing proposals. The argument, unchanged: No canonical key holds *whose record this is* in this role. `our_firm` is the AUTHORSHIP role from 00's consulting sentence (“A consulting document may mention the author’s firm and the client organization.”) and is correctly never destination-eligible; `client` is its role_split partner on the counterparty side; `institution` is the finance-side counterparty a statement or account is held with, not the entity keeping the record; `school`, `lab` and `venue` are other worlds. The concept genuinely unheld is CUSTODY: which entity's operating record a file belongs to. It is the fact that separates a person's employer's board pack from the same person's own limited company's board pack sitting in the same Downloads folder.
proposed_fields.destination_eligible_why: Proposed FALSE, and the tension is stated rather than resolved. Against eligibility: “A folder should not become a collection point for everything produced by the same person or organization.” and the template validator's own prohibition on templates that “use an author or organization merely as a collector” - inside a single-entity corpus an `organization` level is exactly that collector, a one-child level naming the user's own employer above everything. For eligibility: in a corpus that genuinely spans two entities it is the only honest top separator, and “The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions.” means the user can add it themselves. Seeded false so the catalogue never proposes a vanity level; widening is a canonical-list decision, not this row's.
proposed_fields.reliability_why: A letterhead, a footer entity block, or a registered-number slot is a labelled structure a P4 extractor could read as `direct`, but an entity name is exactly the multi-role token 00 warns about - “A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization.” reads across to a company name, which appears as author, employer, customer, supplier, regulator and cited third party. Pinned at `possible` until a gazetteer-plus-context rule family (R4 owns the gazetteer) is authored.

proposed_fields.example: FY2026, Q3 FY26, the 2026-27 planning round
proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: The management calendar of an organisation is a real recurring dimension and no canonical key holds it. `tax_year` is the finance schema's STATUTORY filing year and carries a jurisdiction's meaning; an entity's fiscal year routinely does not coincide with it, and reusing the key would quietly assert that it does. `term` is academic, `application_cycle` is applications, `capture_year` is photos, `creation_date` is when the bytes were made rather than which period the content is ABOUT. Every one of the four rows in this family that cycles annually - budgets, board packs, statutory returns, audits - wants this key and none can have it.
proposed_fields.destination_eligible_why: Proposed TRUE: it is a period, not a person or an author, so 00's “It should avoid using authorship or creator identity as a destination dimension.” prohibition does not reach it, and it is the one level a finance or governance user reliably asks for. It should still not be FIRST - “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.”.
proposed_fields.reliability_why: A `validated` claim is defensible here only because a rule family can confirm it: a fiscal-period token pattern co-occurring with a period-context term in the same labelled block, the same pattern-plus-context SHAPE 00 uses for the academic course code. This row writes no regex and no term list; R2/R6 own those. Without that rule the honest ceiling drops to `possible`.

deterministic: PRECONDITION on every entry below: each is a DETECTION signal and never an extraction licence. This schema declares no field rows, so nothing here writes a domain fact. Detection exists so that the material is recognised, kept local where the row's sensitivity says so, and offered honestly. “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector.”

an entity-identity block: a document whose header, footer, or signature zone carries a registered company or charity name together with a labelled registration-number-shaped token and a registered-office address, in the SAME zone. The entity name alone is never enough (see never_alone); it is the co-occurrence with a labelled registration slot that says 'this is an entity's own formal record' rather than a mention of a company.

a governance-cycle structure: a document carrying a body name, a meeting or period date, and at least two of an attendance list, a numbered agenda, a resolution or decision block, and a papers or pack index. The shape is the CYCLE, and it is what separates this world from a one-off note.

a management-financial table structure: a labelled period column set (budget / forecast / actual / variance, or a period series) over a line-item row set, in a spreadsheet or an embedded table, WITHOUT a bank statement's account-number-and-balance header. “Tables matter because resumes, forms, applications, invoices, and administrative documents often place their most useful information in cells rather than body paragraphs.”

a controlled-document structure: a version, owner, approver, effective-date and review-date header block on a policy, procedure, or standard - the recurring shape of an organisation's governing documents, and one that does not appear on personal papers.

an obligation structure: a numbered clause set with a defined-terms block, a parties block naming two organisations, and an execution or signature block, together with a separate register, schedule, or notice-date table that manages it after signature. The register is the operations-side evidence; the instrument alone is not.

an authority-return structure: a form whose issuing body is a registry, revenue authority, or sector regulator, with a labelled entity-identifier slot, a labelled period slot, and a submission or acknowledgement reference, matched at a word boundary against R4's gazetteer content. R4 owns the gazetteer; this row writes no names.

parent-folder context naming an entity, a department, a fiscal period, or a governance body, treated as a clue that raises plausibility once one of the structures above is already present. Folder context never fires alone.

an email whose labelled sender or recipient slot resolves to a corporate or registry domain and whose labelled subject slot names a period, a body, a contract reference, or a return - and whose attachment-name slot names a pack, a register, a return, or a forecast.

a recurring calendar entry whose labelled SUMMARY names a governance body or a periodic review and whose attendee slots resolve to one organisation's addresses, with a recurrence rule present. “Calendar formats such as ICS should yield event title, start and end time, location, organizer, attendees, and recurrence metadata.” The CONTENT is what fires; source_type = calendar contributes only as a file-kind signal.

an archive whose manifest names a board pack, a due-diligence room export, a policy library, or a period close - read from the manifest alone, because “the normal scan should never extract archive contents to the filesystem”
needs_llm: PRECONDITION: much of this world is commercially confidential and some of it is employee- or customer-identifying, so a model step runs under the user's policy and after P7. “Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default, should not display raw content in general group summaries, and should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it.”

separating the ORGANISATION's side of a document from the INDIVIDUAL's side when both exist. A compensation plan, an offer letter, a policy acknowledgement and an expense claim each exist twice in the world - once as the employer's record (here or `hr`) and once as the person's own (`career`, `finance`). Filenames are identical. This is the central determination for this schema.

separating a REAL operating record from a TEMPLATE, a sample, a course case study, or a downloaded best-practice example. A blank board-minutes template and a real minute are the same document with the values removed, and a consultancy's published example pack is written to look exactly like a real one. “Topic answers what a file is about, while purpose answers what the file was for.”

a purpose-coherent operating packet whose members are individually unremarkable - a board pack carrying a financial appendix, a policy draft, a project status page, a legal note and a slide deck. “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”
unlabelled management prose: a strategy memo, a post-incident write-up, or a customer account note with no header block, no template furniture, and no numbers.
a document in a language whose corporate, governance and regulatory vocabulary the deterministic structure catalogue does not cover.
in every case above, abstention is the required outcome when evidence does not settle it. “A model that cannot cite sufficient evidence must return unknown.”
never_alone: a company, charity, or regulator gazetteer hit alone. 00 states the ambiguity for a university - “A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization.” - and a company name is worse: it appears as employer, customer, supplier, competitor, regulator, letterhead of a document ABOUT the holder, and as an email signature on unrelated material. Stated as inference; 00 writes that sentence about a university, not a company.

business vocabulary alone - strategy, budget, review, stakeholder, governance, roadmap, compliance. An MBA lecture deck, a saved industry article, a job description and a consultancy's marketing PDF are all dense in it and none is an organisation's operating record. This is the tempting false file for this schema.

a slide deck, a spreadsheet, or a numbered-clause document as a SHAPE alone. Every professional world on this roster produces those, which is why each deterministic entry above pairs a shape with a labelled slot.

source_type or extension alone. “treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning” and file_kind_plausible is constitutionally never-alone (CONNECTION section 5, invariant 2).
a bare 4-digit number read as a fiscal year, a company number, a contract number, or a policy version.

a PDF author, producer, or company metadata string alone. “PDF metadata should be treated as supporting evidence, not as truth” - a corporate document template stamps the same company on every blank form it ever generated, including the ones a former employee kept.
membership in a download session that emptied a document-management system or an email thread's attachments at once. “A session should never be treated as proof of topic”
the absence of EXIF as proof that a capture of a dashboard or an intranet page is a screenshot. “the system must not mistake the absence of EXIF for proof that an image is a screenshot”
a parent folder named Work, Admin, Business, or Company alone.

work_types: budget, forecast, reforecast, or variance report
governance meeting notice, paper, pack, minute, or resolution
policy, procedure, standard, or controlled document
project or programme delivery record - plan, status, decision log, retrospective
procurement document - requirement, tender, evaluation, award
contract instrument and the register, notice, and renewal records that run it
customer or partner account record - plan, review, renewal preparation
market, pricing, or product management artifact
compliance evidence, audit report, finding, and corrective action
statutory filing, return, registry document, and the authority's acknowledgement
organisational reference record - registers, org charts, entity documents
grouping_reasons: one governance or reporting CYCLE: the notice, the papers, the pack, the minute, and the actions for one body and one date. Purpose-coherent even where the members share no content. “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”
one project or programme from initiation to closure, across plans, statuses, decisions and the retrospective.
one contract lifecycle: the instrument, its amendments, the register entry, the notices, and the renewal papers.

one customer or supplier relationship over time - and this is the reason most likely to tempt a label copy onto a sparse member, which is exactly what must not happen. “The graph does not automatically copy those missing facts onto sparse files.”
one fiscal period's close across budgets, actuals, returns and the audit evidence that tested them.
one repeatedly re-exported document-management dump, joined by the universal duplicate_family and version_family facts rather than by any business fact.

no group at all is a valid outcome. A single stray policy PDF is an ordinary standalone record and 00's residual library exists precisely for it - “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”
and the stop rules apply here as written: “when members carry irreconcilable course, institution, project, term, or purpose facts” - two entities' returns in one folder do not merge.

template.why: Empty because a dimension may only branch on a field the same schema declares and this placeholder declares none (D1 as narrowed, _CONTRACT rules 10 and 15, CONNECTION PR-6). That is a contract fact, not a judgement that the world has no shape - it plainly does, and it is recorded here as PROSE for whoever answers the open_question. The recommendation, held as prose: the organisational unit or entity only where the corpus really spans more than one (otherwise it is the collector level 00's own template validator rejects - “use an author or organization merely as a collector”), then the governance body, project, contract, or account that the material belongs to, then the fiscal period, then the document function. Not time-first - “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.”. And whatever lands stays a recommendation: “The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions.”

collides_with.signal: The single most load-bearing collision on this row, and the one both sides must state. The SAME document family exists on both sides with the roles reversed: an offer letter, a compensation plan, a policy acknowledgement, an expense claim, a performance review, a consulting statement of work. The discriminating evidence is WHOSE record it is: a document addressed to the holder as an individual, or held to evidence the holder's own employment, standing or engagement, is career; the same document held as the organisation's population-level or counterparty-level record - a schedule of many people, a register, a template, an approval - is this schema. A company name discriminates neither. Where the role does not settle, neither activates: “Correct abstention is a successful outcome because the product’s goal is reliable organization, not maximum file movement.” Provenance: inference.

NJ-J-IND-3 in edge form, and it is a real fork rather than a gap in either row. Money documents split by whether they are a STATUTORY or CUSTODIAL record (an account with an institution, a filed return, a ledger the entity must keep) or a MANAGEMENT artifact (a plan of money that has not happened yet, a variance commentary, a business case). The discriminating evidence: an institution-and-account header, a statutory form's issuing authority, or a double-entry ledger structure supports finance; a period column set of budget / forecast / variance with no account and no institution supports this schema. Both are routinely in one workbook, which is why the fork is recorded as this row's open_question rather than settled here. Provenance: inference.

The two were split on a privacy-rule difference, not a topic one (ROSTER §1b), so the boundary is thin by construction. The discriminating evidence: material that identifies named employees - a case file, a payroll run, a personal review - is hr and must be protected before any model path; material about the organisation's shape, cost and policy WITHOUT named individuals - a headcount budget, a policy, an org chart by role - is this schema. A single spreadsheet frequently crosses that line at one column, and when it does the stricter side wins. Provenance: inference.

Contracts, policies, registers and regulatory correspondence are legal instruments and operational records at once. The discriminating evidence: an executed instrument, a dispute, a tribunal caption, or a privileged advice framing is legal (a safety placeholder that protects first); the register, the notice calendar, the approval workflow and the obligation tracker that RUN it after signature are this schema. Many real files carry both, which is why the pair also holds. Provenance: inference.

An authority's own record and a regulated entity's copy of the same transaction look identical: a permit, a consultation response, a tender, an inspection report. The discriminating evidence is which SIDE the holder is on - an issuing or deciding authority's letterhead, case reference and statutory power supports government; an applicant's or supplier's submission, acknowledgement and evidence file supports this schema. Provenance: inference.

Governance, budgets, policies, procurement and returns are the same objects in a charity, a union, a member association and a company; the ROSTER split them on owner type. The discriminating evidence: a trustee or member-body vocabulary, a charity or union registration slot, a donor or membership record set, and a purpose-of-the-association framing supports nonprofit; a share-capital, customer-revenue and commercial-counterparty framing supports this schema. Neither activates on governance shape alone. Provenance: inference.

A practitioner's corporate-secretarial and contract work produces board minutes, registers and negotiated agreements that are byte-for-byte what the client's own operations file holds. The discriminating evidence: a matter identifier, a client-and-engagement framing, a time-recording or billing anchor, or privileged advice supports law_practice; the same document held by the entity it is ABOUT, with no matter anchor, is this schema. Provenance: inference.

The reciprocal of an edge that family already authored one-way toward this row, restated here so the pair is two-way. Its wording: an organisation's own premises records overlap this schema exactly - a lease of the office, a fit-out project, a facilities contractor, a compliance inspection - and “The discriminating evidence is whether the property is the SUBJECT OF AN INSTRUCTION for someone (this schema) or merely the place the organisation happens to occupy while running itself (business_operations, and specifically its facilities-workplace row).” This row accepts that line without amendment and adds the second half it needs for itself: a construction or property FIRM'S OWN running record - its board pack, its insurance renewal, its staff policy, its year-end pack - is this schema and not that one, because the anchor is the firm running itself rather than a property under instruction. The same fixture bytes on both sides: a fit-out contract for the occupier's own office, which carries a contract sum, a drawing set and valuations (construction_property) and sits in the occupier's contract register under a renewal calendar (this schema). Provenance: inference.

also_holds_with.why: The collision above is the mutex on ONE evidence item; this is the disjoint-evidence case and it is common. A period close carries a management pack and a set of statutory statements in one archive; a budget workbook carries a forecast sheet and a reconciled actuals sheet sourced from an accounting system. Both are true at once on different evidence. finance is a safety schema, so where they co-activate the protective ordering runs first (CONNECTION section 4 step 5). AUTHORED ONE-WAY HERE: the landed finance rows do not name business_operations, and R1c owes the reciprocal. Provenance: inference.

A signed contract in a contract register is one file under two schemas on disjoint evidence - the instrument's execution structure for legal, the register and renewal-notice structure for this schema. legal is a field-less safety placeholder, so the join carries protection on one side and fields on neither. One-way here; R1c owes the reciprocal. Provenance: inference.

A board pack with a workforce appendix, a headcount budget carrying named leavers, a policy library carrying signed acknowledgements: one packet, two schemas, disjoint evidence. hr's privacy posture governs the members that identify people even where this schema activates on the pack. One-way here; R1c owes the reciprocal. Provenance: inference.

The individual's copy of an organisational document is genuinely both: a consulting statement of work is the holder's own engagement record (career, on 00's own “A consulting document may mention the author’s firm and the client organization.” role split) and the delivering organisation's contract record (this schema), on disjoint evidence within one file. One-way here; R1c owes the reciprocal. Provenance: inference.

An IT function's material overlaps a repository's: an architecture decision record, a runbook, a dependency inventory. The repository structure evidences code; the asset register, change approval and compliance-evidence framing evidences this schema. One-way here; R1c owes the reciprocal. Provenance: inference.

falls_through_to.why: The commonest honest home for a standalone operating document with no accepted group - a policy PDF, a certificate, a filed return, a notice. “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”

The right home for a real-looking operating document whose entity, period, or side is unresolved - which in this world is frequent. “Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.”

Isolated transactional members of this world - a purchase confirmation, a filing acknowledgement, a supplier invoice with no register around it. “Receipts and Confirmations may hold isolated invoices, delivery confirmations, booking records, boarding passes, purchase receipts, event tickets, and similar transactional documents.”

Password-protected data-room exports and proprietary system dumps are ordinary in this world. “Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.”

Industry reports, benchmark studies and saved best-practice PDFs are the tempting false files of this schema, and this is where they belong when nothing else fires. “Reading Inbox may hold papers, articles, reports, and saved PDFs that appear to be reading material but have no active research, course, or project association.”

Where an operating file is commercially confidential or carries employee or customer identity - a signed contract, a due-diligence export, a case file - the protective home is the correct one. “Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.”

role_split.why: 00's own role-split pair, and this schema is the second place it bites: “A consulting document may mention the author’s firm and the client organization.” “The agent should model these as distinct facets, such as authored_by and target_school, or our_firm and client.” In this world the same document is filed by the SELLING organisation (its own firm authoring, a client counterparty) and by the BUYING organisation (a supplier counterparty, itself the customer). That third role has no key, which is why `supplier` is proposed on the contract-administration template rather than smuggled in here. Provenance: design for the pair; inference for the reading.

sensitivity_why: Two grounds, both stated conservatively. First, 00's own corpus sentence names material this schema routinely touches - the corpus “can include identity documents, account statements, tax records, medical information, legal records, credentials, private correspondence, GPS metadata, employment materials, and educational records” - and operating files carry employment materials, account statements and legal records as attachments and appendices as a matter of course. Second, and as inference rather than a design claim: much of this world is confidential to a THIRD party - a customer, a supplier, an employer whose material a person keeps on a personal machine - so the exposed party is often not the user and cannot consent to what the product does. That argues for the cautious setting. The handling class is P7's and is not set here.
open_question: Four. (1) NJ-J-IND-3, which this row cannot settle and which the R1c merge needs before the budget-forecast and corporate-regulatory-filings rows can be finalised: where does an ORGANISATION's money live? This row's recorded reading is statutory-and-custodial to finance, forward-looking-management to business_operations, and it is defensible but was drawn by the roster pass rather than by 00. (2) NJ-J-IND-4 for this schema specifically: the row does NOT carry `is_safety_domain` and should not, but its material is frequently third-party confidential, so if the flag stays with 00's four the substitute mechanism that forces P7 ahead of a model path for confidential commercial material must be named somewhere. (3) Whether `organization` and `fiscal_period` may exist as canonical keys at all (proposed_fields, for R1c) - four rows in this family want `fiscal_period` and none can have it, which is the clearest field-shaped hole this pass found. (4) Whether 24 templates on a field-less schema is the right shape, or whether the commercial group (customer-account-management, partnerships-bd, go-to-market, market-research) should collapse toward two rows; this pass's own answer is that each of the four it examined passes the node test on detection signals, with go-to-market the weakest and carrying its own fold question.
